newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-EVANS JOINS BATH AFTER 13 YEARS AT LLANELLI.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-EVANS JOINS BATH AFTER 13 YEARS AT LLANELLI.

text.p: Wales and British Lions winger Ieuan Evans joined Bath from Llanelli on Friday after finalising an unexpected two-year deal on the eve of the transfer deadline for this season's European Cup.

The former Wales captain, his country's top try scorer with 33 tries in a record 71 tests, spent 13 years with his local side but at the age of 33 is now set to embark on a new career in England when he returns from honeymoon in September.

Evans played in seven successive British Lions tests in three tours from 1989 to 1997, culminating in the Lions' victory over South Africa in June before a groin injury -- the latest in a series of setbacks that have bedevilled his career -- cut short his tour.

But despite the fact that Evans, awarded an MBE for his services to the game, is obviously approaching the twilight of an outstanding career, Bath coach Andy Robinson insisted he would be a huge asset to Bath.

"We are all excited about today's news," said Robinson. "Ieaun has been one of the outstanding wings in world rugby for several seasons. The quality of his Lions performances this summer speak for themselves."

Llanelli chief executive Stuart Gallacher said the Welsh club, who Evans led to the league and cup double in 1993 but who now have major financial problems, were "more than happy" with a transfer fee of 75,000 pounds ($119,000). "We wish Ieaun all the best," he said.

Bath had been expected this week to confirm the arrival of Western Samoan winger Brian Lima, but he has yet to appear and the club's England wingers Adedayo Adebayo and Jon Sleightholme are both currently nursing injuries.
Leading rugby agent Mike Burton was among those taken aback by Evans' switch. "I'm surprised. They've got Brian Lima so unless that one's gone down I can't see the point," he said.

"But good Luck to him. It's great to see a bloke like that get something. He's been a great ambassador for Welsh rugby through a not too good period, but the WRU then offered him a derisory contract which didn't reflect what he's done for them as a diplomat.
"He's largely missed the professional era, but now he's getting a few bob and who can begrudge him that?"
